To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the experiences of new migrants in New Zealand are shaped by the social and cultural contexts of the country of settlement, and that the social, cultural, environmental and economic contexts of New Zealand shape the experiences of new immigrants.

“Outdoor nature-based recreation practices in national parks in New Zealand provide a window on contemporary social, environmental and cultural relationships and for new immigrants these relationships parallel their settlement experiences.”
the majority of recent migrants in New Zealand do not participate in outdoor nature-based recreational activities in national parks and regional parks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that outdoor recreation in nature plays in the settlement experiences of immigrants in New Zealand.
the role of nature-based settings in the lives of immigrants and their contribution to the social, economic and political life of the host country.
the social and cultural meanings of nature-based outdoor recreation and the implications for migrants’ integration into New Zealand society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nature of outdoor recreation in New Zealand is changing and this is a reflection of the changes in the social and cultural fabric of New Zealand society.
the research findings demonstrate that the nature of leisure in New Zealand is changing.
for many new immigrants to New Zealand, the ability to locate oneself in nature-based settings, to belong, is central to migrant settlement and integration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nature of leisure in New Zealand is changing and that this is having a profound impact on the way in which people understand and experience the environment and their role within it.
the nature of leisure in New Zealand is not as straightforward as it appears.
the social and environmental values and meanings associated with outdoor nature-based settings are not static but rather are constantly evolving.
The main takeaway from our work is that

for a significant group, recent immigrants in particular, participation in outdoor nature based settings is not always a given and that this raises important questions about the role of these settings in New Zealand society.
the social, cultural and political dimensions of outdoor nature-based recreation are important and need to be taken more seriously in New Zealand.
for some immigrants outdoor nature-based settings provide opportunities to locate themselves within a new environment and to develop a sense of belonging to New Zealand society.
